summary: The 1954 timber tower was moved off the peak in 1976; sources name different buyers, and one diarist's hearsay points to about 1972. A 2025 visit account found six cement footings and outhouse ruins on the summit.

facts.status_note: The 1954 tower was moved off the peak in 1976. firelookout.com says it was sold to a Clark Fork farmer; a 2025 account names a family as the buyer and says most, if not all, of its furniture and windows are now reused in that family's home. The 2025 visit account found six cement footings (four attributed to the 1950s tower) and outhouse ruins on the summit.

visit.trail_note: A visit account posted in September 2025 says the writers hiked in twice, once by the Green Monarch trail and once by a shorter route they call steep.

notes_for_editor: Removal: 1976 in three sources (Forest Lookouts, firelookout.com, and the 2025 account). Buyer conflict: firelookout.com says a Clark Fork farmer; the 2025 account says a family, which the story does not name. Mace's 'after 18 years of service' is hearsay; counting from 1954 gives about 1972, so it is reported as a disagreement. Record height 9.1 m is the 1938 tower; the 1954 tower was 41 ft (see corrections, not applied here). Agency conflict: Mace's 1953 diary places the lookout in the Kaniksu National Forest (Clark Fork District); Forest Lookouts and firelookout.com say Coeur d'Alene National Forest; the record uses Coeur d'Alene. Spelling: the Forest Lookouts page uses 'Shaffer'. Footings: the 2025 account reports six cement footings at the site, four attributed to the 1950s tower and no more than two of the original; an earlier draft wrongly said no source described footings. Staff named only on the 2025 account, not in events or the story: 1949 Bob Kurth and Arnold Krause; 1970 William Phillips. A geocaching listing repeats the 1976 date but was not read or cited. Record events and staffing were empty; staffing lines come from the sources above.
